The Upper Tanana are an Athabaskan people of eastern interior Alaska and the edge of the Yukon, living in villages such as Northway, Tetlin and Tok along the upper Tanana River. Their language is endangered, with fewer than a hundred speakers in 2000.

They lived by hunting caribou and moose, trapping and fishing, and remained remote into the 1900s. In 1942 the Alaska Highway was built through their country, bringing roads, outsiders and epidemics almost overnight. Their neighbours downstream are the Tanana, and to the west the Koyukon.
